memories.memory: I still have about $18,000 left on the mortgage for my house, even though I had expected to pay it off before turning 70.
After retiring from my public-sector management position, my monthly pension is roughly $4,200 before taxes, so I keep a close eye on medical and property-tax costs.
I put $12,000 from my savings into replacing the roof on my home in October 2024 and have been rebuilding that emergency fund ever since.
I co-signed a $9,500 auto loan for my adult son in 2022, and he has been making the payments reliably, but the debt still appears on my credit report.
My former employer overpaid me by about $2,700 during a payroll transition in 2023, and I arranged a repayment plan that deducted $225 from each pension check.
I keep most of my retirement savings in conservative index funds, but I moved approximately $35,000 into cash in early 2025 because I was worried about a market downturn.
I lend my sister $300 a month to help with her utility bills, which has made it harder for me to set aside money for travel.
